title: Given a Scenario, Apply Common Methods for Securing Mobile Devices

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Mobile devices hold personal and corporate data, credentials, email, cloud access, applications, and location information. Protect them with hardening, patching, endpoint security, recovery controls, and policy.
sections.callout: Lock it → encrypt it → patch it → protect it → find it → wipe it → back it up → manage it.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: If a phone or tablet is lost, stolen, outdated, infected, or handling company data, choose the control that protects the device and its information at that stage.

sections.title: Hardening Techniques
paragraphs: Mobile hardening reduces opportunities for unauthorized access or compromise.

entries.title: Device Encryption
paragraphs: Protects data stored on a mobile device so theft does not make the information readable without authentication.
entries.recognitionCue: Stolen phone does not equal readable data.

entries.title: Configuration Profiles
paragraphs: Bundle Wi-Fi, VPN, password, security, email, certificate, and application restrictions into a standard settings package.

sections.title: Screen Locks

entries.title: Facial Recognition
paragraphs: Uses facial characteristics as a biometric unlock method.

entries.title: PIN Codes
paragraphs: Use a numeric or alphanumeric secret; stronger, less predictable PINs provide better protection.

entries.title: Fingerprint
paragraphs: Uses fingerprint characteristics as a biometric unlock method.

entries.title: Pattern
paragraphs: Requires a knowledge-based graphical sequence across screen points and is only as strong as its unpredictability.

entries.title: Swipe
paragraphs: Provides convenience but little meaningful authentication compared with a PIN, password, fingerprint, or face.

sections.callout: Sensitive device → strong authentication, not a simple swipe.

sections.title: Configuration Profiles vs. MDM
paragraphs: A configuration profile is the settings and policy package applied to a device. Mobile Device Management (MDM) is the central platform that distributes, enforces, and monitors those profiles.
sections.callout: Settings package → profile; central management system → MDM.

entries.title: OS Updates
paragraphs: Patch operating-system vulnerabilities and can improve stability, compatibility, and reliability.

entries.title: Application Updates
paragraphs: Patch weaknesses in installed mobile applications.

sections.title: Endpoint Security Software

entries.title: Antivirus
paragraphs: Detects and blocks malicious software; exact capabilities vary by mobile OS and management model.

entries.title: Anti-Malware
paragraphs: Detects or removes a broad range of malicious software.

entries.title: Content Filtering
paragraphs: Blocks or restricts access to dangerous, inappropriate, or unauthorized websites, categories, downloads, and destinations.
entries.recognitionCue: Bad destination or content → filter it.

sections.callout: Antivirus and anti-malware target malicious software; content filtering restricts risky destinations or content.

entries.title: Locator Applications
paragraphs: Use GPS, Wi-Fi, or cellular location to help find a missing device.
entries.recognitionCue: Potentially recoverable lost device → locator application.

entries.title: Remote Wipes
paragraphs: Erase mobile data from a distance when a device is lost, stolen, or no longer under organizational control.

sections.title: Remote Backup Applications
paragraphs: Copy contacts, photos, documents, application data, or configuration to another location so replacing a device does not mean losing authorized data.
sections.callout: Backup preserves the owner's copy; remote wipe destroys the unauthorized local copy.

sections.title: Failed Log-In Attempts Restrictions
paragraphs: Repeated authentication failures can trigger increasing delays, temporary lockout, device lock, or a policy-defined wipe to resist PIN and password guessing.
sections.callout: Repeated wrong credentials → failed-login restriction; inactivity → screen timeout.

entries.title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
paragraphs: Centrally manages configuration profiles, password rules, applications, encryption, remote lock and wipe, compliance, and device restrictions.
entries.recognitionCue: Central control of phones and tablets → MDM.

entries.title: BYOD vs. Corporate-Owned Devices
paragraphs: With Bring Your Own Device (BYOD), the employee owns the device and the organization balances corporate security with personal privacy. With corporate-owned devices, the organization owns the hardware and normally exercises greater control over settings, applications, updates, accounts, and wipe actions.

entries.title: Profile Security Requirements
paragraphs: Define the minimum screen lock, PIN strength, encryption, OS version, application, configuration, and security-software baseline required for corporate access.
entries.recognitionCue: Meet the security profile or do not receive access.

sections.title: Mobile Compliance
paragraphs: A device that does not meet required settings can be restricted, blocked, or remediated before it receives corporate access.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Dangerous website or content → content filtering
Repeated PIN guessing → failed log-in restriction

sections.title: Objective 2.8 Exam Trap
bullets: A screen lock blocks ordinary access; encryption protects the stored data itself.
PIN is something known; fingerprint and face are biometrics.
A simple swipe does not provide strong authentication.
An OS update patches the platform; an application update patches the app.
Antivirus or anti-malware detects software; content filtering restricts risky destinations.
A locator finds a potentially recoverable device; a remote wipe protects data on a stolen or unrecoverable device.
Backup preserves authorized data; wipe removes the local copy.
A configuration profile contains settings; MDM centrally distributes and enforces them.
BYOD is employee owned; corporate-owned means the organization controls the device.
Failed attempts restrictions follow wrong credentials; a screen timeout follows inactivity.

sections.callout: Lock it → encrypt it → patch it → protect it → find it → wipe it → back it up → manage it.
